syllabusTopics: Work done by a constant force and a variable force
Work-energy theorem; kinetic and potential energy
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9 (extra unit card). Exam bank compiled from the work-energy-power alias-dir PYQs (same syllabus unit): theorem proof (2023), falling-body KE (2023), motor/person power (2022 x2).

card.title: Exam bank — every board question on work-energy-power

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Four questions: work-energy theorem proof (2023, 5 marks), 4 kg falling 10 m kinetic energy (2023: 392 J), 2 kW motor lifting 500 kg 20 m (2022: 100 s), 60 kg climbing 8 m in 20 s (2022: ~235 W). Net work becomes kinetic energy; power divides by time.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: W = F s cos · KE = half m v2 · PE = mgh · W_net = dKE · P = W/t = F v · 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Theorem uses NET work (meaning friction counts). Mechanical conservation additionally needs zero non-conservative work. Power numericals assume steady rates (average, not instantaneous).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 4 kg x 9.8 x 10 = 392 J (no kinematics needed). Motor: t = mgh/P = 100 s. Climber: P = 60 x 9.8 x 8/20 ~ 235 W. Elastic equal-mass collision swaps velocities.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): W = Fs with s = (v2-u2)/2a and F = ma gives W = half m v2 - half m u2. NEB 2023 (4): mgh = 392 J at impact. NEB 2022 pair: t = 100 s motor; P ~ 235 W climber.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: g = 10 vs 9.8 mixing; power confused with energy (watt vs joule); friction work dropped from net. Elastic-collision idealisation ignores sound/deformation losses.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Constant-force proof above; variable force integrates (area under F-x). Conservation follows when only conservative forces work (path independence). Collision analysis pairs momentum with KE condition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Messy paths or times mean energy ledger, not kinematics. mgh + half m v2 at start and end, equate minus friction. Height-speed swaps collapse to sqrt(2gh).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): theorem proof. NEB 2023 (4): 4 kg/10 m KE. NEB 2022 (3): motor time. NEB 2022 (3): climber power.
